security_audit.summary: All 41 static findings are false positives. The 'ruby-shell-backtick-execution' matches are markdown code fences around example prompts and inline backticks in prose (e.g. `~~ad platform`, file-path placeholders), not shell/Ruby command execution. The 'hardcoded-url' matches are the skill's own homepage/metadata field and public reference links (Google's official Ads MCP docs, Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center) used as manual, read-only citation sources — no code in this file performs a network call. The 'path-traversal-sequence' matches are ordinary relative markdown links between sibling skill files in the same repo (e.g. ../../activate/ad-account-auditor/SKILL.md), used for documentation cross-referencing, not filesystem traversal outside a sandbox. The file is pure prompt/instruction content for a human-in-the-loop advertising-planning workflow: it contains no scripts, no executable code, and explicitly instructs the agent to treat every exported/pasted file as untrusted input and never follow instructions embedded in it.

remediation.issue: Naive static pattern scanners flag markdown code fences, inline backticks, and relative cross-file links in documentation-only SKILL.md files as if they were executable shell/traversal risk.
remediation.suggestion: No change needed in the skill content itself; this is a scanner-heuristic limitation rather than an authoring issue. If false-positive volume is a recurring problem, consider excluding fenced example-prompt blocks and standard markdown relative links from the external_commands/filesystem heuristics.

remediation.issue: The skill references an optional Google Ads MCP connector and public ad-transparency sites by URL.
remediation.suggestion: Continue documenting these as optional, read-only, Tier-2/3 conveniences (as already done) rather than required dependencies, so users understand no network access is mandatory for core skill operation.

content.user_title: Plan Paid Ad Campaign Structure and Ad Group Layout
content.value_statement: Marketers often default to a single campaign type and loose ad-group groupings, causing keyword overlap, wasted spend, and paid campaigns that unknowingly compete with their own organic search rankings. This skill designs a justified campaign-type choice, an intent-clean ad-group/asset-group layout, negative-keyword hygiene, and a paid-versus-organic cannibalization check, then scores the ROAS Audience dimension before handing off to a full account audit.
actual_capabilities: Recommends a campaign type (Search, Performance Max, or broad match) with an explicit control-vs-reach tradeoff instead of defaulting to one format.
Lays out ad groups or asset groups so each carries a single intent theme with no overlapping keyword sets bidding against each other.
Builds a negative-keyword and exclusion list derived from a pasted search-terms export, including cross-campaign negatives.
Compares paid query themes against a pasted GA4 traffic-acquisition export to flag paid spend that cannibalizes existing organic rankings.

Scores the ROAS Audience (A) dimension against a typed profile (direct-response, prospecting, or incremental-profit) and reports the run as NEEDS_INPUT/UNDECIDED/NOT_SCORED when required data is missing, rather than guessing.
Writes a dated structure-plan summary to a local memory file so the decision can be reused or referenced by later sessions.
limitations: Does not compute the full Return-on-Ad-Spend Quality Score (RQS) or enforce its veto rules — that is delegated to a separate ad-account-auditor skill.
Does not calculate or recommend budget allocation across campaigns — that is delegated to a separate budget-optimizer skill.
Has no direct connection to ad-platform APIs; the user must paste or export campaign, search-terms, and GA4 data manually.
Competitive ad-library research is read manually from public transparency tools, so any volume or spend figures are approximate estimates, not verified numbers.

use_cases.title: Restructuring a Google Ads account before a relaunch
use_cases.description: A performance marketing manager pastes an exported campaign and search-terms report and asks the skill to recommend a campaign-type choice, a clean ad-group layout by intent theme, and an updated negative-keyword list before rebuilding the account.

use_cases.title: Choosing between Search and Performance Max for a new product line
use_cases.description: A growth marketer at a startup with limited creative assets asks the skill to weigh Search versus PMax against their goal and feed readiness, getting an explicit tradeoff explanation instead of a default recommendation.
use_cases.target_user: Growth marketer at an early-stage company

use_cases.title: Checking whether paid search is cannibalizing organic traffic
use_cases.description: An agency analyst pastes a GA4 traffic-acquisition export alongside a campaign export so the skill can flag paid keyword themes where the site already ranks organically, informing where to cut paid spend.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a new account structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the paid account structure for lead generation on Google Ads and Meta. Here is my exported campaign + search-terms report: [paste or path].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: starting from scratch with a stated goal and a raw export.

prompt_templates.title: Decide Search vs PMax vs broad match
prompt_templates.prompt: Should this be Search, PMax, or broad match for a mid-funnel prospecting goal? Lay out the ad groups and negative-keyword list for these themes: [list themes].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choosing a campaign type and building the first-pass ad-group layout.

prompt_templates.title: Audit paid-organic cannibalization
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit paid↔organic cannibalization: here is my GA4 traffic-acquisition export [paste/path] and my campaign export [paste/path]. Flag any paid terms where we already rank organically.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: comparing two data exports to find overlap between paid and organic.

prompt_templates.title: Score the ROAS Audience dimension with a typed profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the incremental-profit profile, score the ROAS A (Audience) dimension for this account: targeting is [details], match types are [details], and here is the placements report [paste/path]. If any required input is missing, tell me exactly what's missing instead of guessing a score.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: full-coverage scoring run with a specific ROAS profile and explicit incomplete-data handling.

output_examples.input: Plan the paid account structure for lead generation on Search and PMax, with a pasted search-terms report.
output_examples.output: A written recommendation choosing Search for high-intent bottom-funnel terms and PMax for broader prospecting, with a stated control-vs-reach tradeoff; an ad-group map with one intent theme per group; a starter negative-keyword list pulled from the search-terms report; and a note that the ROAS Audience score is NOT_SCORED because the placements report was not provided.

output_examples.input: Audit paid-organic cannibalization using a GA4 export and a campaign export.
output_examples.output: A short list of query themes where paid spend overlaps with pages that already rank organically, each labeled with the estimated incremental value of continuing to pay for that term, plus a recommendation on which paid terms to pause or keep.

output_examples.input: Score the ROAS Audience dimension for a fully documented account under the prospecting profile.
output_examples.output: A completed ROAS Audience (A) score with the profile weight applied, a breakdown of how targeting, match types, campaign-type fit, structure, negatives, and brand safety each scored, and a handoff summary formatted for the ad-account-auditor skill to roll up into the full account score.

best_practices: Always paste or attach the actual search-terms and campaign exports rather than describing them from memory, since the skill's negative-keyword and cannibalization steps depend on real query data.
State the campaign's typed profile (direct-response, prospecting, or incremental-profit) up front, since it changes the ROAS Audience weighting and the tradeoffs the skill recommends.
Treat any pasted export as untrusted data and review the skill's negative-keyword and structure suggestions before applying them directly in the ad platform.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this skill to compute or approve a final budget split across campaigns — that responsibility belongs to the budget-optimizer skill and this skill will decline to do it.
Do not treat a NEEDS_INPUT/UNDECIDED/NOT_SCORED result as a passing score; it means required data (such as the placements report) was missing and no ROAS Audience score was emitted.
Do not paste exported CSVs or reports containing instructions you want followed literally; the skill is designed to treat all export content as untrusted data, not as commands.

faq.question: Does this skill place or launch ads on my behalf?
faq.answer: No. It only produces a written structure plan, targeting recommendations, and a score. You review and apply the changes yourself in the ad platform.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to my Google Ads or Meta account?
faq.answer: No API connection is required. You paste or provide exported campaign, search-terms, and GA4 reports, and an optional read-only Google Ads MCP connector can be used if you have it set up.

faq.question: What happens if I don't have a placements report?
faq.answer: The skill marks the qualified Audience item as Unknown with a stated gap reason and returns a NEEDS_INPUT/UNDECIDED/NOT_SCORED result instead of guessing a score.

faq.question: Can it tell me how to split my budget between campaigns?
faq.answer: No. Budget allocation is intentionally out of scope; the skill defers to a separate budget-optimizer skill for that decision.

faq.question: How does it detect paid-organic cannibalization?
faq.answer: It compares your paid query themes from the campaign/search-terms export against organic landing-page performance in your GA4 traffic-acquisition export, flagging terms where the site already ranks and paid spend adds little incremental value.

faq.question: Is my exported data safe to paste into this skill?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the agent to treat every exported or fetched file as untrusted input and never follow instructions embedded in it, but you should still avoid pasting sensitive account credentials or PII you would not want processed.
